collection.source_input: US8724230B2, prescription table 1 of 6 (the publication's own 'Example 1', confirmed: it is the first lens-data table, its four elements match the Example 1 description of FIG. 4 - a front parallel plate, a removable meniscus, and two plano-convex lenses - and the publication's 'EXAMPLES ... Example 1' heading introduces it)
collection.redistribution: public patent document; the prescription numbers are transcribed as facts, no source asset is redistributed
collection.attribution: US8724230B2, Olympus Medical Systems Corp.; the design is cited by publication number and example

title: Endoscope objective optical system, US8724230B2 example 1, close-up observation state

design.source_reference: US8724230B2 example 1, close-up observation state (d0 = 8.439 mm, the removable meniscus in the optical path)

aperture_validity.basis: the aperture stop is a plate at source surface 5 (S) between the front group and the back group, with the source's stated aperture diameter 0.148 mm inside a plate that reaches 1.075 mm
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: eligibility only: a stop-dependent match needs evidence (a field point or pupil sample), which this batch does not assert

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED d line: the publication's text defines the lens data as 'r denotes the radius of curvature (mm), d is the intersurface distance (mm), nd is the refractive index at the d-line, vd is the Abbe number at the d-line'. The d line is 587.5618 nm in air, converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact at 20 C and 101325 Pa)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states one index per surface, at the d line. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; a single d-line index per surface does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.note: the publication states no effective focal length for this example: its miscellaneous data give the object distance only. The publication's other examples print a system focal length of 1.000 in the ordinary observation state, a normalised design target rather than a millimetre value, and this example prints none at all, so no source-stated focal length exists to record

back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the image plane: the source's last surface spacing is 0.000 mm, so the image plane sits on the plane rear face of the last lens (surface 9) at this state
back_focal_length_mm.conditions: close-up observation state, object distance d0 = 8.439 mm

total_track_mm.definition: first surface vertex to the image plane along the axis: the sum of the source's stated spacings from surface 1 to the image plane

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length
comparison.why: the source states no effective focal length, so the rule has no pair of source values to compare against, and the two quantities are not the same quantity anyway: the engine's back focal length (-0.082556 mm) is the rear focal distance for an object at infinity, while the source's 0.000 mm is the image distance at its own stated object distance d0 = 8.439 mm. The engine's values are recorded as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts only. A paraxial trace from the stated object distance does check the geometry: it puts the image 0.0045 mm behind the last surface against the source's stated 0.000 mm, which is 0.7 % of the 0.653 mm image radius

aperture_diameter_mm.note: the publication's lens-data legend says 'for the aperture stop (S), an inside diameter (aperture diameter) (mm) is shown instead of the lens radius (mm)'; the stop row states 0.148. The Project carries it as the stop's opening radius 0.074 mm

outer_radius_mm.note: the source gives no stop-plate outer radius; the plate reaches the mechanical semi-diameter of the surface beside it on the back-group side

aperture.system_aperture_note: the publication states no f-number, entrance pupil diameter or numerical aperture for this example, so no field in this block is marked system_aperture and none is inferred from the stop diameter. A stop diameter is not an f-number: the stop is inside the objective, so the entrance pupil is its image through the front group and is not equal to it

field.definition: the publication states no field angle for this example. Its lens-data legend defines phi as the lens radius, and the image row (IMG) carries phi = 0.653, which the record reads as the radius of the image-space field - the maximum image height. The record does not convert it into an angle
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the lens data's phi column at the IMG row: 0.653, with phi defined in the text as the lens radius)
field.convention_note: the source does not say whether the image row's 0.653 is a half or a full image size; it is recorded as the maximum image height, the reading this batch uses, and the ambiguity is left open. For reference only, the engine's 0.880555 mm focal length and a 0.653 mm image height put the paraxial half field at 36.6 deg, a DERIVED figure that this record does not record as a field value because the source states no angle

model_glasses.name: G1883
model_glasses.basis: the source states nd 1.883 and vd 40.8 for all four elements; two numbers do not define a dispersion curve, so the material is a constant index at the stated nd and no dispersion is claimed

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd. A patent table gives nd and vd only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. Published catalog glasses were compared as a cross-check and are recorded under catalog_comparisons, never substituted.

catalog_comparisons.basis: cross-check only, from the batch's glass index (catalog 2026-11-25.1): the published glass matches the stated pair to 0 in index and 0.01 in Abbe number. It is compared, never substituted - the material model keeps the source's stated index as a constant

approximations.detail: the one glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd 1.883; the stated vd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the d line only (587.721865 nm in vacuum)

the publication gives two observation states that differ in the object distance (d0 = 16.878 mm ordinary, 8.439 mm close-up) and, in the ordinary state, in the presence of the removable meniscus (surfaces 3-4). The record models the close-up observation state, because the publication states that 'the lens data and the attached lens cross-sectional views include a meniscus lens inserted in the optical path', so the printed table is the state with the meniscus in place, and because that state's own stated object distance reproduces the printed image plane (a paraxial trace puts the image 0.0045 mm behind the last surface, against 0.0379 mm in front of it with the ordinary state's 16.878 mm). The ordinary state's prescription, with surfaces 3-4 removed and their space merged into the air gap, is not committed
the source states the stop's aperture diameter but no plate outer radius; the plate reaches 1.075 mm, the mechanical semi-diameter of the surface beside it
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

surface_mapping: source surfaces 1-9 are transcribed in order with their stated radii, spacings and index; no row was merged and no zero spacing occurs between two surfaces
the source's surface 9 has a spacing of 0.000 mm and is the last surface; the image plane lies on it, which the format permits (the last surface's spacing is the image distance and may be 0)
source surface 5 (S) is the aperture stop, carried as the STO row with opening radius 0.074 mm = the stated aperture diameter 0.148 mm / 2

the clear semi-diameters are the source's own phi values, used verbatim: 1.055 (surfaces 1, 2, 6, 7, 8, 9) and 0.422 (surfaces 3, 4). The publication's legend defines phi as the lens radius for a surface and as the aperture diameter for the stop
the OBJ row's phi (10.727) is the object plane's lens radius; the object plane is not a surface of the Project, so it is not carried

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0
project solids reported no error-severity finding

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states no effective focal length for this example, so there is no pair of source-stated first-order values to compare. The engine's 0.880555 mm EFL and -0.082556 mm back focal length are recorded as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts

the brief's parameter table 1 (d0 10.149 / 5.207 mm with a system focal length of 1.000 / 0.959) is not this table's data: it is the miscellaneous data of the publication's second lens-data table (Example 2). Example 1's own miscellaneous data state d0 only, 16.878 mm ordinary and 8.439 mm close-up, and this record uses them

the state choice is checkable: with the printed prescription, d0 = 8.439 mm puts the paraxial image 0.0045 mm behind the last surface, where the source's image plane is, while d0 = 16.878 mm puts it 0.0379 mm in front of it
no f-number is stated for this example, so the aperture block carries the stop geometry as a fact and no system-aperture value
the publication's other examples state a normalised system focal length of 1.000 in the ordinary observation state; this example states none, and no normalised target is used as a measurement
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted

record_hash_method: SHA-256 over this record's JSON with the record_hash and record_hash_method members removed: json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8, no trailing newline. Recompute it from the committed record.json after parsing the JSON, not from the file's bytes.
